requirements.statement: Provide an optional, replaceable booking email library with Gmail search and retrieval as the first connector. Each deployment supplies its own dedicated inbox and read credentials. Use an opaque plus tag per booking for exact lookup and authorized manual access to original messages. Retrieve candidate messages and trusted provenance for separate LibCal verification; keep mailbox configuration, credentials, original messages and cancellation links private and caller-owned. A deployment may leave email disconnected. Booking submission remains available, and confirmation requires independent trusted evidence.
requirements.plain_language: Find booking mail in the deployment’s own inbox using the complete booking address. The caller supplies read access and trusted source information; finding a message alone does not confirm a reservation. This keeps deployments separate and lets an authorized operator find the original safely. If you leave email disconnected, you can still submit a booking and track any status supported by other trusted evidence.
requirements.positive_example: A synthetic deployment binds rooms@example.invalid to its injected connector and looks up rooms+opaque17@example.invalid. It returns only messages addressed to that exact tag, with independently supplied provenance for later receipt checks; an authorized operator uses the saved reference to find the same original privately.

acceptance.statement: Document the optional Gmail retrieval interface, the interface for alternate mailbox providers or push delivery, and which existing protected-source retrieval behavior (public technical description: docs/email.md) is reused. Keep mailbox configuration and credentials supplied by the caller.

Use a dedicated inbox and read credentials per deployment. Exercise mailbox isolation with synthetic bindings, including an inaccessible or wrong inbox, and prevent fallback to another deployment’s mailbox.

Use an opaque plus tag per booking. Exercise exact complete tagged-recipient lookup and rejection of similar tags; document how an authorized operator locates the original message manually using the same saved booking reference.

Retrieve candidate messages and trusted provenance for separate LibCal verification. Exercise duplicate and out-of-order messages without treating routing matches or message order as proof of confirmation.

Exercise actionable access, timeout and verification failures with synthetic fixtures. Keep original messages and cancellation links private; safe diagnostics must support recovery without exposing them.

Retain the source distinction: a manual provider test reported a submission receipt with its plus tag intact, while API search and follow-up delivery remain unverified until separately observed. Synthetic fixtures do not establish live delivery or compatibility.
With email disconnected, allow booking submission without mailbox access. Report confirmation only when other trusted evidence verifies the exact booking, and leave email-only updates unavailable.

requirements.statement: Document and exercise a synthetic consumer from tagged booking submission through deployment-specific email lookup and verified status. Use a distinct inbox and credentials per deployment, authorized operator access to originals, actionable missing/inaccessible/ambiguous evidence, and safe member updates. The calling application owns member authorization, in-site updates, optional email preferences and delivery. Distinguish submitted, provider-reported pending reservation, confirmed and needs attention; keep original receipts and cancellation links out of member updates.
requirements.plain_language: Show how an application connects a booking request to its mail and status without exposing the receipt. Members may request rooms only when the app permits it; operators resolve mail problems. Separate “sent,” “awaiting provider approval,” “confirmed,” and “needs attention” so members know what happened.
requirements.positive_example: An authorized member requests a room while creating a synthetic event. The saved tag lets an authorized operator retrieve the original from that deployment’s inbox. A trusted pending receipt shows awaiting approval; an exact verified approval shows confirmed. The site and opted-in status email show only safe status text, while the original and cancellation link stay private.
